original_question: Let Kn be the Kasteleyn matrix of the Aztec diamond of order n in which every other vertical domino has its sign flipped. Prove that the sum of the entries of K_n^{-1} equals (n-1)(n+3)/2 - 2^(n-1) + 2.
target_in_paper: Section 3 ("Dominoes"), Problem 12 of Twenty Open Problems in Enumeration of Matchings.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the Aztec-diamond setting, the use of the inverse of the signed Kasteleyn/Kasteleyn-Percus matrix, and the exact closed-form expression that Problem 12 asks one to prove.
missing_details: The paper's matrix is specifically the Kasteleyn-Percus matrix, i.e. a signed bipartite adjacency matrix, not an unspecified Kasteleyn matrix.
The underlying graph is the bipartite graph dual to the Aztec diamond region of order n.
A fixed checkerboard coloring must be chosen.

The sign convention is not merely "every other vertical domino": one negates exactly those entries corresponding to vertical dominos whose white square is on top relative to that fixed checkerboard coloring.
Equivalently, in the bipartite adjacency matrix one replaces the corresponding 1-entries by -1; the other nonzero entries remain +1.
Rows are indexed by white vertices/squares and columns by black vertices/squares.
The quantifier "for every positive integer n" is implicit in the paper and should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone version.
The phrase "sum of the entries" should be made explicit as the sum of all entries of K_n^{-1}.
The inverse is the ordinary matrix inverse of this square matrix; the paper leaves the coefficient field implicit.
In the paper this is posed as an open problem/conjectural identity, with the note that the formula was checked for n = 1, ..., 8; the draft omits that status/context.
refined_question: For each positive integer n, let K_n be the Kasteleyn-Percus matrix of the bipartite graph dual to the Aztec diamond of order n, with rows indexed by white vertices and columns by black vertices under a fixed checkerboard coloring, and with the sign convention that each nonzero entry corresponding to a vertical domino whose white square is on top is replaced by -1 (all other nonzero entries remaining +1). Prove that the sum of all entries of K_n^{-1} is ((n-1)(n+3))/2 - 2^(n-1) + 2. As stated in the paper, this identity has been verified for n = 1, ..., 8.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's Problem 12: it asks for exactly the same inverse-matrix entry-sum formula for the Aztec diamond. The paper's nearby context makes the intended matrix more precise: Percus' determinant is defined as a signed bipartite adjacency matrix, and Section 3 explains the Aztec-diamond/domino setting via the dual bipartite graph and checkerboard coloring before stating Problem 12 with the exact sign rule. arXiv also records that math/9801060 was later superseded by math/9904150, whose text preserves this formulation.
